build.notes:
CLEAN M=1 CAVEAT (the entanglement IS the localization, per the task's guidance): conv1d (depthwise causal, width 4) and the GDN scan (recurrent) are STATEFUL/CONTEXTUAL. The native kernels consume query rows in FLAT order, so a deep-row-ALONE M1 arm cannot reproduce the deep node's query-side ancestry (its ancestors are not present as query rows; only the prior-window remains) -> M1 is RECEPTIVE-FIELD-REDUCED. I therefore made the clean co-residency control M10-vs-M5 (branch rows present vs absent, deep node's spine-ancestry context identical, since for cat9 the spine slice == the deep node's ancestry), and recorded M5-vs-M1 as the receptive-field axis with an explicit m1_receptive_field_caveat in every record. A large M5-vs-M1 with M10-vs-M5 ~0 localizes the carrier to the stateful receptive field, NOT a batch-tile occupancy effect.

EXPECTED RESULT (from the concurrent FR13_CONV_FIX_DESIGN.md committed at b6c30b4b, which I read): the tree-conv emulation is ROW-OCCUPANCY M-INVARIANT by construction (per-row Python loop, NO cross-row reduction), so conv1d_out M10-vs-M5 should be ~0. The real surviving carrier is num_accepted-driven AND the our-kernel-vs-native bf16-tap/silu realization seam (~9.77e-4 born at L0 from byte-exact pre_conv) — which is why I added the served_fused_vs_native_decode metric. This MAB will EMPIRICALLY confirm/refute row-occupancy M-invariance and separate it from the realization seam.

Tree ENGAGED correctly: container log shows "FR13_TREE_CONV_FUSED conv emulation engaged: tree_n=10 width=4" immediately before the crash, so the hook's class-9 engagement asserts (tree_n==10, path0/parent present) PASSED — it got past them into the kernel re-run.

ROOT CAUSE (located, not guessed): the hook's observe-only GDN sub-op A/B re-run launches a kernel that triggers a device-side assert. First assert surfaces INSIDE the hook ("FR13_GDN_SUBOP_MAB A/B failed: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered" at gdn_linear_attn.py:909, the hook's try/except). The hook catches it, but a CUDA device-side assert irreversibly poisons the SHARED CUDA context, so the live forward's NEXT kernel (fused_post_conv_prep -> _fused_post_conv_kernel, gdn_linear_attn.py:3938/fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py:215) also faults and the EngineCore dies (HTTP 500, EngineDeadError). The M10 (full-tree) arm uses geometry IDENTICAL to the live call (idx=range(tree_n), unchanged ssi0/nacc) so it cannot be the source; the OOB is in the M5/M1 receptive-field-reduced arms whose state-index geometry is sliced/reordered: scan-arm ssm_state_indices=ssi0.index_select(1, idx) + num_accepted_tokens=nacc.clamp(max=m) + inplace_final_state=True (state STORE path, fused_sigmoid_gating.py:171-180), and/or the conv-arm causal_conv1d_update with the same clamped num_accepted. The broad try/except + Triton lazy-assert hide the exact failing line; even blocking only confirmed the hook is the first faulter.

The observe-only contract is VIOLATED de facto: a device-side assert in the re-run cannot be isolated from the live forward on a shared context, so this hook can crash the served engine even though every arm uses detached clones.

FIX NEEDED (next GPU boot): correct the M5/M1 arm state-index geometry so the re-run kernels never OOB. I drafted then REVERTED a candidate (num_accepted_tokens=None + inplace_final_state=False + ssm_state_indices=None) because with ssm_state_indices=None the scan reads initial_state at flat position bos=0 instead of the deep node's bank slot — that would silently corrupt the h0 and yield decoherent/misleading numbers (worse than a loud crash per the 'math-correct != bit-exact / scalar-metric-blindspot' lessons). verdict.causalChainRedTeam:
Born-at-L0 test FAVORS conv over the overturned FA2 — but does NOT rescue it as the flip carrier. QPAD failed because the forked-FA2 query-tile is DOWNSTREAM: first full-attn is L3, so a tile fix at L31 (QPAD target) could not remove a divergence already 2-bf16-ULP at L0 (7.8125e-3, node7 ladder ladder_summary.json), and e2e flips stayed 24. The conv1d_out IS genuinely upstream/born-at-L0 (pre_conv 0.0 -> conv1d_out is the FIRST nonzero sub-op at the carrier event), so by the L0-origin argument fixing it COULD in principle propagate. THAT is the only sense in which conv beats FA2.

BUT the argument that fixing conv WOULD drop the 22 flips FAILS on two independent grounds, and I cannot make it: (1) ROW-OCCUPANCY M-INVARIANCE — the tree-conv is a per-b loop with no cross-row reduction (fr13_tree_conv_fused.py:200-249), so the deep-spine conv arithmetic does NOT depend on how many branch rows are co-resident. The 22-vs-5 (cat9-vs-chain5) gap is "branches add ~17 via spine-perturbation" (11/11 ch2 flips ON spine); an M-invariant op cannot be that carrier. (2) ALREADY-AT-FLOOR — the bf16-tap + ex2.approx-silu replica is the LIVE path (FR13_GATEA: conv front DONE, silu grind succeeded); the surviving conv delta is at most sub-ULP, and the concurrent CPU conv-mechanism verify (wf_d27ad02e) returned holds=True / wouldFixReduceFlips=False. So conv satisfies the L0-origin test yet is the WRONG knob: it is the entry POINT of the diffuse accumulation, not its DRIVER. The real driver (scan state-feed chunk-vs-recurrent) scales with accept DEPTH, which reconciles branches-add-17 as deeper-accept = longer rank-1 chain = more chunk-vs-recurrent accumulation. CONCLUSION: a conv fix would very likely also fail to move the flips (like QPAD), for a DIFFERENT reason than QPAD (QPAD=downstream; conv=upstream-but-M-invariant-and-already-aligned). A reshape fallback (shallower spine + root-sibling width) is the indicated path because it attacks the depth-accumulation driver directly rather than any single op — and this run produced NO co-residency number to overturn that, so the diffuse/reshape disposition stands unrefuted, not confirmed.
